There's another metric that no one talks about: fractional reserve banking. Since I have no idea how much the current multiplication rate is, I'll make up a simple number: 100. The multiplication rate is how many dollars a bank can make out of thin air when it gets a physical dollar in its vault. So if you deposit your paycheck of, say, $500 at a multiplication rate of 100, the bank can now make $500,000 out of nothing.

The $499,999 dollars have no value (fiat currency) so what's this "money supply" you talk about? That's right, the ability for banks to borrow money. If the Fed makes it too easy for banks to borrow, they'll lend out to people and businesses too quickly and you get hyperinflation - useful if you want to pull an economy out of a recession because the only way out of a recession is to spend money and you can't do that if you don't have it. But if you're not in a recession and you have money to burn, inflation happens and waterfalls into hyperinflation. So the Fed raised the interest rates. For you, that means high interest on your credit cards. For the banks, it means it costs more to borrow money. It also means that inflation drops. But it also stalls an economy if done too quickly or at the wrong times.
